title: How to update zoom on Mac: step by step for Zoom Workplace on macOS
metaTitle: How to Update Zoom on Mac: Steps for Zoom Workplace
description: Learn how to update Zoom on Mac with Check for Updates, turn on automatic updates, and fix the 10004 install error in Zoom Workplace.
targetKeyword: how to update zoom on mac
intro: To update Zoom on Mac, open Zoom Workplace, sign in, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, and choose Check for Updates. If a newer version exists, Zoom downloads and installs it, and you can also turn on automatic updates so you stop checking by hand.
tldr: Open Zoom Workplace, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, then click Check for Updates.
Zoom downloads and installs a newer version. Mandatory updates block you until the install finishes.
To stop checking by hand, open Zoom > Settings > General and tick Automatically keep my Zoom up to date.
MSI installs have no Check for Updates button, so contact IT or your Zoom account admin.
For Unable to install updates, error code 10004, follow MacPaw's fixes, starting with status.zoom.us.

blocks.text: Zoom updates matter for security as much as for new features. BleepingComputer reported that Zoom patched more than a dozen medium and high severity flaws in the two months before it launched automatic updates for Windows and macOS desktop clients. That history is a good reason to keep the app current, not just to click Update once and forget it.
Which Zoom app you are updating

Zoom's current help calls the desktop app Zoom Workplace. Older guides say Zoom, and some still point to a zoom.us item in the menu bar. Zoom's own support article names the profile picture route and does not name that menu bar item, so start with the profile picture. I could not find a dated Zoom note that explains the rename, so treat both names as one product.

The browser version is a separate question. The help article I checked covers the desktop client across several platforms, including macOS. If you join meetings from a browser without installing anything, this page does not describe a browser update, and I could not confirm whether a browser client needs one.
Check for Updates from the profile menu

Zoom's support article describes one route for the desktop app. You sign in, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, and click Check for Updates. If a newer version exists, Zoom downloads and installs it. The article treats this as a step inside the app, so you do not need to hunt for a new installer.

Zoom also checks for updates on its own. According to the same article, a pop-up appears for new mandatory or optional updates within 24 hours of login. You do not have to wait for that pop-up. If you want the update now, run Check for Updates yourself.

A mandatory update blocks you until it is done. An optional update can be postponed. Zoom prompts you again at your next login, so a postponed update does not vanish. Plan to install optional updates at a quiet moment rather than in the middle of your day.

Say you are in a client call when an update finishes downloading. Zoom's blog says that if an update is ready during a meeting, you are prompted after the meeting ends. The update waits until the call is over, so your meeting is not interrupted.
Turn on automatic updates so you stop checking

Automatic updates are available on Windows and macOS desktop clients. Linux is not supported. Zoom's blog says to open Settings, go to the General section, and tick Automatically keep my Zoom up to date. Admin credentials come up only when you enable the setting, so have them ready if the Mac is managed.

BleepingComputer reports that a Zoom security product manager said automatic updates would be on by default for most individual users. Those users can opt out after their first install or update, under Zoom > Settings > General. If you have never looked at that setting, check it once. The default may already be on for you.
Slow or Fast: which update channel to pick

Zoom's blog describes two update channels. Slow is the default, and it focuses on stability with less frequent updates. Fast lets you adopt new features and updates as soon as they are available. Critical security updates go to all users regardless of the channel you pick.

Here is how I would choose. Stay on Slow if you run client meetings and cannot afford surprises during a call. Pick Fast if you want new features early and can handle more frequent changes. Either way, security fixes still reach your Mac.

Zoom's blog says it publishes client updates monthly, with out-of-cycle releases when needed. Expect a regular rhythm, plus the occasional update that arrives between cycles. Even with automatic updates on, a quick manual check now and then is cheap insurance.
Work-managed Macs and MSI installs

If the desktop app came from an MSI package, Zoom's article says AutoUpdate is off by default. The Check for Updates button is also removed for those installs. Those users must contact IT or the Zoom account admin. I could not find the same rule for a Mac .pkg install, so check with IT if your Mac is managed.

Ask before you reinstall anything on a work Mac. A reinstall can clash with how IT set up the app, and you may not have the rights to finish it anyway. A short message to IT can save you a long troubleshooting session.
When the update will not install

One error people search for on Mac is code 10004, which reads Unable to install updates. MacPaw's guide on this error was last updated April 24, 2024. It is a third-party guide, not a Zoom page, and I could not find a Zoom page for this error.

Start with the status page at status.zoom.us before you touch the app. Reinstalling will not help if Zoom has a service problem. If the status page looks normal, work through the fixes in the order listed below, from the least invasive step to the most invasive one.

Keep macOS current too. MacPaw lists updating macOS as one of its fixes, so it belongs on your checklist before you reach for safe mode. Following MacPaw's order lets you stop as soon as the update installs.
Check your version against the newest release

A third-party tracker, Releasebot, lists macOS Zoom Workplace 7.2.5 (build 90525) dated October 31, 2026 as the newest release. Earlier entries include 7.2.2 on September 24, 2026, and 7.2.0 on September 18, 2026. The tracker also lists 7.1.9 for the Slow track only.

Use that list as a rough target, not a final answer. Releasebot is a third-party tracker, and I could not check it against Zoom's own release notes. If your version is older than the newest one listed, run Check for Updates. If it matches, you are probably current.
Common mistakes to avoid

Looking for Check for Updates on an MSI install and giving up. The button is removed on those installs, so the fix is a message to IT, not more clicking. Give the IT team your version and install type, and they can move faster.
Postponing an optional update and forgetting it. Zoom asks again at your next login, but a long gap between logins means a long gap without fixes. Set a reminder if you rarely sign out of Zoom.
Treating a tracker's version number as Zoom's final word. Releasebot can help you spot a stale install, but Zoom's own notes are the source to trust for what changed in each release.
What to do after the update

After the install, reopen the app and join a short test meeting with your camera and microphone on. If camera access fails, use the matching guide. Camera permissions are handled in System Settings, and this guide walks through them: [grant camera access in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom).

Screen sharing depends on permissions too. The screen share guide covers desktop steps, shortcuts and black screen fixes: [share your screen in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-zoom). Read it before a client call if sharing matters to you.

If you cannot use automatic updates, make it a habit to run Check for Updates after each sign in. If you can use them, leave the setting on and check the version now and then. Either way, you have a clear route to the newest Zoom on your Mac.

faq.question: Where is Check for Updates in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: Click your profile picture in the top-right corner of the Zoom Workplace window, then click Check for Updates. MSI installs do not have that button, so ask IT or your Zoom account admin instead.

faq.question: Does Zoom update itself on a Mac?
faq.answer: Only if you turn on automatic updates. Open Settings, go to General, and tick Automatically keep my Zoom up to date. Zoom asks for admin credentials only at that point. Zoom also shows a pop-up for new updates within 24 hours of login.

faq.question: Can I postpone a Zoom update on Mac?
faq.answer: Optional updates can be postponed, and Zoom prompts you again at your next login. Mandatory updates block you until the install finishes, so you cannot postpone those.

faq.question: What does Unable to install updates, error code 10004 mean?
faq.answer: MacPaw's guide describes this error on Mac. Check status.zoom.us first, then uninstall Zoom Workplace, restart, and install the .pkg from zoom.us/download that matches your chip. I could not find a Zoom page for this error.

faq.question: Which version of Zoom is the newest for Mac?
faq.answer: A third-party tracker, Releasebot, lists macOS Zoom Workplace 7.2.5 (build 90525) dated October 31, 2026. Releasebot is not Zoom, and I could not check it against Zoom's release notes.

faq.question: Does automatic updating work on Linux?
faq.answer: No. Zoom's blog says automatic updates are available on Windows and macOS desktop clients, and Linux is not supported.

faq.question: Do I need to update Zoom to join from a browser?
faq.answer: I could not confirm this. The help article I checked covers the desktop app, and no page I opened says whether the browser version needs an update.

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace and sign in
steps.text: Open the Zoom Workplace app from the Dock or your Applications folder, then sign in with your Zoom account. Zoom's update steps start from the signed-in desktop app.
steps.tip: No app yet? Get the installer from zoom.us/download, Zoom's own Download Center.

steps.name: Click your profile picture
steps.text: Look at the top-right corner of the Zoom window and click your profile picture. Zoom's support article names this corner, not the menu bar.

steps.name: Click Check for Updates
steps.text: In the menu that opens, click Check for Updates. If a newer version exists, Zoom downloads it and installs it for you.

steps.name: Let the download and install finish
steps.text: Keep the Mac on and connected until Zoom finishes. A mandatory update blocks the app until it is done, so plan the install for a quiet moment.
steps.tip: If a meeting starts while the update is ready, Zoom prompts you after the meeting ends.

steps.name: Check the version you now run
steps.text: Open the app screen that shows your version, then compare it with the newest release listed by a tracker. I could not confirm the exact Mac menu for that screen, so read the labels in your window.

steps.name: Turn on automatic updates
steps.text: Open Settings from the Zoom menu, choose General, and tick Automatically keep my Zoom up to date. Zoom asks for admin credentials only when you enable it.
steps.tip: Automatic updates are not supported on Linux. Zoom's blog covers Windows and macOS desktop clients.

steps.name: Pick the Slow or Fast channel
steps.text: Slow is the default and focuses on stability. Fast gets new features as soon as they are available. I could not confirm the exact Mac menu for switching channels, so check the General section and read the labels.
steps.tip: Critical security updates reach everyone, whichever channel you choose.

troubleshooting.problem: Check for Updates is missing from the profile menu
troubleshooting.fix: Your install may be an MSI package. Zoom says auto-update is off and the button is removed for MSI installs. Contact IT or your Zoom account admin.

troubleshooting.problem: Unable to install updates, error code 10004
troubleshooting.fix: Check status.zoom.us first. Then choose Zoom menu > Uninstall Zoom Workplace, restart, and install the .pkg from zoom.us/download for your chip, Intel or Apple silicon. Check your chip under the Apple menu, About This Mac.

troubleshooting.problem: The install still fails after reinstalling
troubleshooting.fix: Grant Full Disk Access in System Settings under Privacy & Security, then update macOS and try again. MacPaw lists both as fixes.

troubleshooting.problem: Safe mode seems like the only option left
troubleshooting.fix: MacPaw suggests updating in safe mode only after the other fixes fail. Restart your Mac in safe mode, run the update, then restart normally.

troubleshooting.problem: An optional update pop-up keeps coming back
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom asks again at your next login if you postpone an optional update. Install it at the next quiet moment so the prompt stops.
